intro: Use a comparative to compare two things: tall → taller. Use a superlative to show the top one in a group: tall → tallest.

sections.title: Short adjectives: -er and -est
sections.text: For many short adjectives, add -er or -est: tall → taller → tallest. If the word ends in -e, add -r or -st: large → larger → largest. Double the last letter in short words such as big → bigger → biggest.
examples: My bag is bigger than your bag.
This is the largest room in the school.
sections.note: Do not double w, x or y.

sections.title: Adjectives ending in -y
sections.text: For easy, busy, noisy, happy and heavy, change y to i: easy → easier → easiest. But shy keeps y: shy → shyer → shyest.
examples: This question is easier than the last one.
The canteen is the noisiest place at school.

sections.title: Longer adjectives and two correct forms
sections.text: Use more and most with longer adjectives: more careful; the most interesting. With quiet, clever, narrow and simple, two forms can be right.
examples: This map is more useful than the old map.
This is the simplest way home.
This is the most simple way home.
sections.note: Both listed forms are accepted in this course.

sections.title: Irregular forms and far
sections.text: Good → better → best. Bad → worse → worst. For distance, use farther/farthest or further/furthest. Both are correct.
examples: This bus route is better than the old route.
This is the farthest shop from our school.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.text: Use one pattern only: easier, not more easier; the fastest, not the most fastest.
examples: The second question is easier than the first.
She chose the most interesting book.

sections.title: Than, the, good and well
sections.text: Use than after a comparative: cleaner than the old desk. Use the before a superlative adjective and a noun: the cleanest desk. Use good before a noun. Use well to say how someone does something.

miniCheck.sentence: The school hall is _____ than our classroom.
miniCheck.explanation: Large ends in -e, so add -r: larger.

miniCheck.sentence: Of the three bags, the red bag is the _____.
miniCheck.explanation: Good is irregular: good → better → best.

miniCheck.sentence: This is the _____ place in the library.
miniCheck.explanation: Use quietest. The most quiet is also correct, but it is not an option here.
